newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ terms of trade continue to fall in June qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ terms of trade continue to fall in June qtr.

text.p: New Zealand's terms of trade continued to fall in the June quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Wednesday.
The index fell 0.7 percent from the March to June quarters and was 0.8 percent lower than in the June 1995 quarter.
On an annual basis, the index decreased 1.4 percent. However, the index is still 10.2 percent higher than it was during the 1980s, the department said.
The June quarter fall was the result of a 2.1 percent fall in export prices combined with a 1.4 percent fall in import prices.

An 8.6 percent fall in dairy prices, 8.5 percent fall in forest products, 5.6 percent fall in casein, 3.5 percent decline in wool and 1.6 percent decline in aluminium were the main factors behind the fall in the export index, SNZ said.

Export prices were affected by a stronger dollar in the June year. On a trade-weighted basis, the New Zealand dollar strengthened 0.6 percent from the March to June quarters and is now 6.4 percent higher than in the June 1995 quarter.

Export volumes for the June quarter were 6.2 percent higher than a year ago with dairy volumes up 21.7 percent and fish up 9.1 percent. Volumes in forest products were down 1.0 percent and were down 6.1 percent in wool.

Import prices fell 1.4 percent from the March quarter and are now 0.7 percent lower than in the June 1995 quarter. In the latest quarter, petroleum products were down 9.2 percent, textiles and fabrics were down 4.3 percent and transport equipment was down 2.7 percent.
Import volumes were 4.8 percent higher in the quarter and 0.1 percent higher than in June 1995.
The volume index for capital goods rose 2.3 percent in the quarter but was 20.4 percent lower than in the June 1995 quarter, which included substantial aircraft imports.
